items.title: Section: Dependent Origination Closes — Arising, Cessation, and Mode Three Complete

items.zh: 復更尋求：如是先行何依何緣？既尋求已，如實悟入：如是先行依緣無明。如是了知無明依緣先行，先行依緣命根，命根依緣身心，身心依緣入息、出息。又能了知無明滅故行滅，行滅故命根滅，命根滅故身心滅，身心滅故入出息滅。如是名為悟入緣起。彼於緣起悟入多住，名善習修。是名悟入緣起修習。
items.en: Inquiring further still: on what does this prior karmic action depend, and what is its condition? Having inquired, one truly realises: this prior karmic action depends on and is conditioned by ignorance. Thus one comes to know: ignorance conditions prior karmic action; prior karmic action conditions the life faculty; the life faculty conditions body and mind; body and mind condition the in-breath and out-breath. And one further comes to know: with the cessation of ignorance, karmic action ceases; with the cessation of karmic action, the life faculty ceases; with the cessation of the life faculty, body and mind cease; with the cessation of body and mind, the in-breath and out-breath cease. This is called realising dependent origination. Dwelling extensively in this realisation is called thorough cultivation. This is cultivation through realising dependent origination.

items.title: Section: The Four Noble Truths Open and Close as Mode Four

items.zh: 如是彼於緣起悟入善修習已，復於諸行如實了知從眾緣生，悟入無常。謂悟入諸行是無常故，本無而有，有已散滅。若是本無而有，有已散滅，即是生法、老法、病法、死法。若是生法、老法、病法、死法，即是其苦。若是其苦，即是無我，不得自在，遠離宰主。如是名為由無常、苦、空、無我行，悟入苦諦。又彼如是能正悟入諸所有行眾緣生起，其性是苦，如病、如癰，一切皆以貪愛為緣。又正悟入即此能生眾苦貪愛若無餘斷，即是畢竟寂靜微妙。我若於此如是了知、如是觀見、如是多住，當於貪愛能無餘斷。如是名能悟入集諦、滅諦、道諦。於此悟入能多住已，於諸諦中證得現觀。是名悟入聖諦修習。
items.en: Having thoroughly cultivated the realisation of dependent origination, one further truly knows that all conditioned formations arise from conditions, and realises impermanence … which is subject to birth, ageing, sickness, and death … which is suffering. Being suffering, it is without self, lacking autonomy, free of any controlling master. This is realising the truth of suffering through the aspects of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. … All of this has craving as its condition. … And truly realising that this craving which produces every suffering, once cut off without remainder, is itself final, tranquil, and sublime peace [realises the truth of cessation]. … If I come to know this, to see it directly, and to dwell in it extensively, craving will be cut off without remainder [realising the truth of the path]. This is realising the truths of origin, cessation, and path. Dwelling extensively in this realisation, one attains direct insight into the truths. This is cultivation through realising the noble truths.

items.title: Section: The Sixteen Excellent Practices Open — the Fifth and Final Mode

items.zh: 如是於聖諦中善修習已，於見道所斷一切煩惱皆悉永斷，唯餘修道所斷煩惱。為斷彼故，復進修習十六勝行。
items.en: Having thoroughly cultivated realisation within the noble truths in this way, all afflictions abandoned at the path of seeing are permanently cut off; only the afflictions abandoned at the path of cultivation remain. In order to cut these off as well, one further advances into cultivating the sixteen excellent practices.

items.title: The Sixteen Excellent Practices, Part One: Body and Feeling

items.zh: 謂於念入息，我今能學念於入息；於念出息，我今能學念於出息。若長、若短。於覺了遍身入息，我今能學覺了遍身入息；於覺了遍身出息，我今能學覺了遍身出息。於息除身行入息，我今能學息除身行入息；於息除身行出息，我今能學息除身行出息。於覺了喜入息，我今能學覺了喜入息；於覺了喜出息，我今能學覺了喜出息。於覺了樂入息，我今能學覺了樂入息；於覺了樂出息，我今能學覺了樂出息。於覺了心行入息，我今能學覺了心行入息；於覺了心行出息，我今能學覺了心行出息。於息除心行入息，我今能學息除心行入息；
items.en: Regarding mindfulness of the in-breath: I now train myself to be mindful of the in-breath. Regarding mindfulness of the out-breath: I now train myself to be mindful of the out-breath — whether long or short. Regarding awareness of the in-breath pervading the whole body: I now train myself in this awareness … Regarding calming the bodily formation on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding awareness of joy on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding awareness of bliss on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding awareness of the mental formation on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding calming the mental formation on the in-breath: I now train myself in this …

items.title: Section: Mind and Dharma Close the Sixteen Practices — All Five Purifying Objects Complete

items.zh: 於息除心行出息，我今能學息除心行出息。於覺了心入息，我今能學覺了心入息；於覺了心出息，我今能學覺了心出息。於喜悅心入息，我今能學喜悅心入息；於喜悅心出息，我今能學喜悅心出息。於制持心入息，我今能學制持心入息；於制持心出息，我今能學制持心出息。於解脫心入息，我今能學解脫心入息；於解脫心出息，我今能學解脫心出息。於無常隨觀入息，我今能學無常隨觀入息；於無常隨觀出息，我今能學無常隨觀出息。於斷隨觀入息，我今能學斷隨觀入息；於斷隨觀出息，我今能學斷隨觀出息。於離欲隨觀入息，我今能學離欲隨觀入息；於離欲隨觀出息，我今能學離欲隨觀出息。於滅隨觀入息，我今能學滅隨觀入息；於滅隨觀出息，我今能學滅隨觀出息。
items.en: Regarding awareness of the mind on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding gladdening the mind on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding restraining and steadying the mind on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding liberating the mind on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding contemplating impermanence on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding contemplating abandonment on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding contemplating dispassion on the in-breath: I now train myself in this … Regarding contemplating cessation on the in-breath, I now train myself in this; regarding contemplating cessation on the out-breath, I now train myself in this.

blocks.text: The famous **sixteen excellent practices** of breath meditation, here placed after stream-entry, as a path to cut the remaining afflictions.

"With the cessation of ignorance, karmic action ceases; with that, the life faculty ceases; … the in- and out-breath cease." Thus "ignorance conditions prior karma; prior karma, the life faculty; the life faculty, body and mind; body and mind, the breath."

Seeing that all formations arise from conditions, one realises impermanence; "being impermanent, it is suffering; being suffering, it is without self, lacking autonomy". Dwelling in this, one attains direct insight into the truths: stream-entry.

After stream-entry, "only the afflictions abandoned on the path of cultivation remain". To cut them, one cultivates sixteen practices, in four groups of four (matching the four foundations of mindfulness): - **Body**: mindful of the in-breath and out-breath, long or short; aware of the whole body; calming bodily activity. Venerable Miào Jìng: between in- and out-breath there is no breath, and that is "calming". - **Feeling**: experiencing joy, experiencing pleasure, aware of mental activity, calming it. - **Mind**: aware of the mind, gladdening it, steadying it, liberating it. - **Phenomena**: contemplating impermanence, abandonment, dispassion, cessation.
Each is practised "I now train myself in this", on the in-breath and on the out-breath.

quiz.q: How does the cessation side of dependent origination run, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say one thereby penetrates?
options: with ignorance ceasing, action ceases … with body and mind ceasing, breath ceases; one penetrates both the origination of saṃsāra and that of nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "With the cessation of ignorance, karmic action ceases; with the cessation of karmic action, the life faculty ceases … the in-breath and out-breath cease." Venerable Miào Jìng: one penetrates the dependent origination of birth and death, and also that of nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: Earlier one traced back from breath to ignorance; here it runs ignorance → action → … → breath. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the direction?
options: the earlier inquiry traced backward; here it is stated the other way, with the same meaning
quiz.why: "Thus one comes to know: ignorance conditions prior karmic action; prior karmic action conditions the life faculty; the life faculty conditions body and mind; body and mind condition the in-breath and out-breath." Master Cháng Bǎi: the earlier inquiry traced dependent origination backward from the end; stated the other way round, the meaning is the same.

quiz.q: "One attains direct insight into the truths." On what basis does Venerable Miào Jìng judge this to be the first fruit?
options: the earlier pliancy was access concentration, not the first or second form absorption
quiz.why: "Dwelling extensively in this realisation, one attains direct insight into the truths." Venerable Miào Jìng: the earlier bodily and mental pliancy was access concentration, not the first or second form absorption — so this is the first fruit attained on that basis.

quiz.q: Why cultivate the sixteen excellent practices, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say the path of seeing cuts off?
options: the seeing-path afflictions are cut, only cultivation-path ones remain; seeing cuts mainly self-view, rule-attachment, doubt — greed and hatred remain
quiz.why: "All afflictions abandoned at the path of seeing are permanently cut off; only the afflictions abandoned at the path of cultivation remain." Venerable Miào Jìng: mainly self-view, attachment to rules, and doubt — of the five lower fetters, greed and hatred are not yet cut.

quiz.q: The note says "calming the bodily formation" is the mid-interval pause. What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: the place between in- and out-breath has no breath at all — that is calming the bodily formation — and he rejects equating it with the mid-interval breath; Cháng Bǎi equates them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: between in- and out-breath there is no breath at all — neither in nor out — and that place is "calming the bodily formation." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is truly knowing the mid-interval in- and out-breaths. Yet §10 defines the mid-interval breath as a faint wind-like stirring, which conflicts with his reading.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "awareness of the in-breath pervading the whole body"?
options: the in-breath enters through every pore; ordinary people breathe this way too but are not aware of it
quiz.why: "Regarding awareness of the in-breath pervading the whole body: I now train myself in this awareness." Venerable Miào Jìng: the in-breath comes through every pore of the body; ordinary people are like this too, but they are not aware of it.

quiz.q: In "gladdening the mind on the in-breath," what does Venerable Miào Jìng say the pure, excellent object is?
options: the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha — the most excellent objects of one's reverence and praise
quiz.why: "Regarding gladdening the mind on the in-breath: I now train myself in this." Venerable Miào Jìng: the pure, excellent object is the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha — the most excellent, what one reveres and praises. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise links it to the six recollections.
